subject: Post-demo follow-up: SLO targets, streaming needs, and proposed bench plan
messages:
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Amy Lee <amy@edgescale.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: SLO targets, streaming needs, and proposed bench plan

Hi Amy / Kunal —

Thanks for a productive demo earlier. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed to confirm on the call: 

1) Target SLOs you asked us to validate in the qualification run:
   - P95 latency <= 150ms for short-form responses (~<64 tokens)
   - P95 latency <= 350ms for long-form responses (~512 tokens)
   - Sustained concurrency target: 2,000 concurrent requests (steady-state)
   - Burst tolerance: spikes to 3,500 concurrent for up to 2 minutes with graceful shedding
   - Streaming: partial token flush every ~80ms (progressive delivery) for chat UX

2) Workload characterization we need from EdgeScale to build the harness:
   - Representative prompt bundle (1k examples across instructions, clarifications, code, and multi-turn chat)
   - Token length distribution (short / medium / long) and expected generation lengths
   - Acceptance criteria: latency bands + minimal quality drop (we'll use rouge/bertscore for automated checks)

3) Proposed bench methodology (draft we discussed):
   - Use Redwood eval harness (attached instructions) with your prompt bundle (please share)
   - Measurement windows: 15-minute steady-state runs, repeated 6 times over different times of day
   - Metric outputs: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tail-token latency for streaming, tokens/s and user-perceived time-to-first-byte

4) Deliverables & owners:
   - EdgeScale: share prompt bundle + token distribution (Amy) — due Wed 12/16
   - Redwood: publish bench config + measurement definition doc (Kimberly) — due Fri 12/18
   - Redwood infra contact for deeper perf tuning: Karthik (CC'ed)

Attachments: a stub prompt bundle template and a suggested SLO matrix.

If these items look right I will: (a) drop the harness instructions into a shared Drive folder, (b) schedule a short kickoff with Karthik and your infra lead, and (c) start the initial runs once we have the bundle.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: SLO targets, streaming needs, and proposed bench plan

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 2,000 concurrency number is client-side connections; our infra maps that to ~1,600 active model requests given front-end batching. Can you confirm the harness will allow both request-level and connection-level modelling?
- For streaming, we care most about time-to-first-token (TTFT) for the mobile SDK. Our target: TTFT < 120ms p95 and partial token delivery cadence around 80–100ms.
- Quality checks: we can provide 200 human-eval labels for a subset of prompts; the rest can be automated.

We will share:
- Prompt bundle (anonymized) by EOD Wed 12/16 (Amy)
- A small infra runbook showing how our gateway aggregates requests (Kunal) by Thu 12/17

Also looping in our infra lead to the kickoff — tagging them on the kickoff invite once you schedule.

Best,
Amy Lee
Head of Product, EdgeScale Inc

Amy / team — quick technical notes from our side before we ingest the bundle: 

- Harness will model both connection-level and request-level concurrency. We'll add a translation layer to approximate front-end batching to match EdgeScale's gateway behavior (Kunal's runbook will help tune that).
- Measurement defs we'll use (sending this early so expectations align):
  * Request latency: time from request headers sent to final token emitted (p50/p90/p95/p99)
  * TTFT (time-to-first-token): from request send to first token flush (important for mobile)
  * Streaming cadence: median inter-token flush intervals during generation
  * Effective throughput: tokens/s measured at model runtime, and user-level throughput measured as completed responses/minute
- Reproducibility: all runs will be stored with seed, model version, quantization profile, and kernel selection. We will publish the run manifest in the shared Drive.

Two asks for EdgeScale to make runs repeatable:
1) Provide deterministic prompt IDs in the bundle (a stable key per example)
2) Include a small sticky-session sample (10 requests) that exercises multi-turn context reuse so we can validate KV-cache effects

I'll sync with Neha on the eval definitions once we get the bundle.

— Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
